title: Sections of an etale sheaf of sets over a strictly henselian local open are its stalk
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U\subseteq T$ an open subscheme with an isomorphism $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] for a strictly henselian local ring $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] whose image is the point $u\in U$ corresponding to $\mathfrak m$. The inclusion $j:U\to T$ is etale, so $(U,\bar t)$ (with $\bar t$ regarded as a morphism to $U$) is a pointed etale neighbourhood of $\bar t$ [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods]. Then for every sheaf of sets $G$ on $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] the germ map $G(U)\to G_{\bar t}$, $a\mapsto$ the germ of $a$ at $(U,\bar t)$ (stalk of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]), is bijective. (For $U=T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ this is Stacks 03QO for sheaves of sets; its abelian version is lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk.)

proof.text: For a pointed etale neighbourhood X of the given geometric point, pull X back to U and compose its etale projection to U with the isomorphism U ≅ Spec R. Shrink the marked point to an affine open Spec B. Write phi : R → B for the etale algebra map and q for the image of the marked geometric point. The equality over Spec R and the closed-point hypothesis give q ∩ R = maximalIdeal R. This is the affine reduction in Stacks Tag 03QO, carried out by the private helper exists_pointed_section_spec.

The localization B_q is weakly etale over R, since B is etale and localization is weakly etale. The equality q ∩ R = maximalIdeal R proves that R → B_q is a local homomorphism. Apply Olivier's theorem (Stacks Tag 092Z), Algebra.WeaklyEtale.bijective_of_isStrictlyHenselianLocalRing, to obtain an isomorphism er : R ≃ B_q. The composite B → B_q → R defines the section. To verify the marked geometric point, let chi : B → Ω be its ring map and theta : R → Ω the base geometric point's map. Every element outside q has nonzero image under chi, so chi extends to chi_q : B_q → Ω. The identity chi_q ∘ er = theta implies theta ∘ er⁻¹ ∘ (B → B_q) = chi. Applying Spec shows equality of geometric morphisms, not merely equality of their points. Transport the section back to U and project from the pullback to X. The private helper strictlyHenselianOpen_pointedSection packages the resulting pointed morphism U → X.

Use Mathlib's pointSmallEtale and GrothendieckTopology.Point.toPresheafFiber_eq_iff', whose filtered-colimit equality criterion uses cofilteredness of the category of pointed etale neighbourhoods. If two sections of G(U) have the same germ, they agree after restriction along f : Y → U. Choose a pointed section g : U → Y by step 2. Since U.ι is a monomorphism and f and g are over T, g ≫ f = id_U. Applying G(g) to the equality and functoriality proves the original sections equal. For surjectivity, GrothendieckTopology.Point.toPresheafFiber_jointly_surjective represents a germ by a section a over a pointed neighbourhood X. Choose f : U → X by step 2. The section G(f)(a) has that germ by toPresheafFiber_w_apply. Thus the stated germ map is bijective. The argument in fact works for every presheaf; no sheaf condition is used.

tool_uses.why: Affine pointed-neighbourhood shrinking is a generic etale-site tool used to represent an arbitrary germ.
The finite separability of residue extensions for etale morphisms is used to trivialize the marked residue field.
The separably closed residue field turns the finite separable residue extension into an isomorphism; this generic field lemma is in another unit.
The henselian simple-root lifting criterion supplies the lift used in the etale retraction.
The lifted root is packaged as the retraction of the etale algebra, a generic henselian tool from another unit.
Cofilteredness of N_tbar is required by the hypotheses of the initial-full-subcategory colimit lemma.
Cofinality of the singleton identity-neighbourhood subcategory is the categorical reduction of the stalk colimit.
The reduced singleton colimit is computed as a constant connected diagram.
